profile_text.body:
NVIDIA Research is the research arm of NVIDIA, based in Santa Clara, California, and described in its own materials as a for-profit research lab. Its site says it is focused on developing technology and finding breakthroughs, and it points visitors to an AI Playground where demos from its research teams can be tried, along with a set of open-source resources intended to simplify programming tasks for AI researchers.

Those resources include NVIDIA Sionna, Kaolin, Kaolin Wisp, Imaginaire, and CUDA-X. The site describes Kaolin as a PyTorch library that accelerates 3D deep learning research through differentiable 3D modules and a curated model zoo of 3D deep learning architectures. CUDA is described as a parallel computing platform and programming model developed by NVIDIA for general computing on GPUs, with CUDA-X a collection of libraries for AI and high-performance computing built on top of CUDA. The company also offers NVIDIA AI Foundation Models, which it describes as an interface for trying curated and optimized AI models in a browser, running on the NVIDIA accelerated computing stack.

A litigation record associated with the company lists 281 cases in California. No products, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for it.
